Existing methods for constructing descriptors of a given response tensor are limited to first-order multipole expansions or restricted to simple magnetic structures. In this work, we construct a complete symmetry-invariant descriptor basis for arbitrary crystal structures and magnetic textures, providing interpretable features for machine learning modeling of response tensors. item.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Piotr Białas, Christian D. Morales, Tomasz Stebel, Dawid Zapolski
arXiv:2610.23783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to 96×96, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.

item.title: Reconstruction of Magnetic Fields with a Physics-Informed Neural Network
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 P. Adhikari, R. Bhattarai, J. Brewington, D. Buskirk, F. B. Hills, Md F. Hossain, R. McDonald, P. A. Palamure, A. Reid, S. Sharmin, A. Tewsley-Booth, B. Plaster
arXiv:2610.23691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate reconstruction of magnetic fields and their gradients is essential for assessing and controlling systematic effects in precision measurement experiments. We have developed a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method which reconstructs three-dimensional magnetic fields subject to the source-free Maxwell equations, nablaḑotB=0 and nabla×B=0. In an extension of our previous work on PINN methods for reconstruction of magnetic fields in inaccessible interior regions via measurements at exterior locations, we now demonstrate the feasibility of applying PINN methods to the extraction of magnetic field gradient terms from discrete measurement points subject to constraints from Maxwell's equations.

item.title: Training Dataset Matters for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: Water Simulation as an Example
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yifan Li, Bingjia Yang, Chunyi Zhang, Axel Gomez, Pinchen Xie, Yixiao Chen, Pablo M. Piaggi, Roberto Car
arXiv:2512.23939v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate predictions of machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) rely on training datasets covering relevant thermodynamic conditions and phases. Using water as an example, we show that insufficiently sampled datasets of MLIPs lead to wrong predictions of densities, melting temperatures, and nuclear quantum effects. In contrast, MLIPs trained on comprehensive datasets with the same electronic structure method yield consistent property predictions agnostic of MLIP architecture, with densities in quantitative agreement with reference calculations.

item.title: Magnetic-field-free parity-protected qubit based on a narrow altermagnet Josephson junction
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Sakineh Vosoughi-nia, Michał P. Nowak
arXiv:2510.18145v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnets provide a new route to engineer superconducting circuits without magnetic fields. We theoretically study the Andreev bound state (ABS) spectrum of a finite-width altrmagnet-based Josephson junction and show how the d-wave altermagnetic symmetry and geometric confinement shape its low-energy excitations. We find a clear distinction between the two d-wave symmetries: dₓ^₂₋y^₂ order produces spin splitting, whereas dₓy order preserves spin degeneracy and exhibits splitting of the ABS spectrum induced by intermode hybridization. Leveraging these novel features, we propose applying a transverse electric field to tune the system and realize a magnetic-field-free, parity-protected superconducting qubit that we call altermon.

arXiv:2608.13483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thin-film Mn₅Si₃ is a prominent altermagnetic candidate owing to its metallicity, demonstrated anisotropic anomalous transport, and proposed d-wave exchange splitting that could enable spin-polarized transport.
